project.name: taiyishenshu
project.description: Tai Yi Shen Shu (太乙神数) is a Flutter/Dart application that implements three schools (Jinjing, Tongzong, Jicheng) of the classical Chinese Tai Yi divination system, computing year/month/day/hour chart algorithms (积年, 局数, 阴阳遁, 太乙宫, 文昌/计神, 主客算, 八门, 天/神盘星神, 格局, 九贵神) and presenting them via multiple UI styles (classic radial grid, compass-style grid, standard 3×3 nine-palace grid).

tour.title: Project Overview & AI Governance
tour.description: Start with the README to learn that this project is a Flutter implementation of Tai Yi Shen Shu (太乙神数), supporting three classical schools — Jinjing (金镜派), Tongzong (统宗派), and Jicheng (集成派) — and four chart types (year/month/day/hour). AI_README.md and the CONSTITUTION add the project's AI-collaboration rules and design philosophy: algorithm/UI separation, no third-party state library, and JSON-driven school configuration. Read these first to anchor the rest of the tour in the project's own narrative.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: lib/main.dart boots the Flutter app and hands routing to lib/navigator.dart, which wires the top-level page tree. This is the smallest possible app shell: no DI container, no router package — just a MaterialApp pointing at TaiyiPanPage. Notice how main.dart sits at the apex of the BFS traversal (depth 0) and reaches everything else through just two depth-1 imports: the page and the theme.
tour.languageLesson: Dart's `main()` is the entry function. `runApp()` inflates a Widget tree and binds it to the Flutter engine — there's no equivalent of React's separate root.render() because Flutter owns the rendering loop directly.

tour.title: State Layer — ChangeNotifier Wiring
tour.description: TaiyiPanController is the single source of truth for chart state. Instead of pulling in Provider, Riverpod, or Bloc, the project deliberately uses Dart's built-in ChangeNotifier and a plain Listener — honoring the CONSTITUTION's 'no third-party state library' rule from Step 1. The controller owns the date/time inputs, the selected school, and the computed PanDataModel, and notifies listeners whenever the user changes a parameter so the page rebuilds.
tour.languageLesson: ChangeNotifier is Dart's minimal observable: subclasses call `notifyListeners()` to trigger any widget that subscribed via `addListener()` or `AnimatedBuilder`. It costs zero dependencies but requires manual `dispose()` to avoid leaking listeners.

tour.title: Domain Enums — The Vocabulary of Tai Yi
tour.description: Before reading any algorithm, learn the vocabulary. `gong.dart` (九宫 — the nine palaces) is the most fan-in-heavy node in the entire codebase (20 incoming edges), making it the single most important type to understand. `door.dart` (八门), `god.dart` (神), and `taiyi_enum_extensions.dart` add the eight doors, deity catalog, and Chinese-name helpers. These enums turn opaque integer indices from classical texts into self-documenting names used everywhere downstream.
tour.languageLesson: Dart enums can carry constructor fields and methods, so each Gong value can store its Luoshu number, palace name, and Chinese label. Extension methods (in taiyi_enum_extensions.dart) attach helpers without subclassing — a clean way to layer presentation labels onto pure-domain enums.

tour.title: Pan Data Models — Five Boards of the Chart
tour.description: A Tai Yi chart is built from five 'pans' (boards) stacked together: tian (天 sky), di (地 earth), ren (人 human), shen (神 deity), and ming (命 destiny). Each model is a plain Dart data class describing what gets rendered at one layer of the radial grid. Following the depth-3 BFS layer reveals that the controller from Step 3 ultimately produces these five structures via the aggregate PanDataModel from Step 7.

tour.title: Algorithm Strategy Pattern — Encoding School Differences
tour.description: This is the architectural keystone. The three schools (金镜/统宗/集成) disagree on many specific computations — yang-yin escapement direction, which palace hosts Taiyi, how the eight doors rotate — and AlgorithmEngine plus AlgorithmSpec wrap those differences as a strategy. SchoolConfig is the data side: it tells the engine which DeityDefinitions and rule profiles to load for the current school. Together they make 'pick a school' a single line of configuration instead of three forked code paths.
tour.languageLesson: The strategy pattern in Dart is typically implemented as abstract classes plus const factory configs rather than full interface/impl pairs. `_RuleProfile` (mentioned in the README) is a private class — Dart's library-level privacy means underscore-prefixed identifiers are only visible within the file, giving you encapsulation without needing a separate `internal` keyword.

tour.title: Core Calculator — The Heart of the System
tour.description: TaiyiPanCalculator is the largest single file in the project (~1700 lines) and runs the full algorithm chain the README describes: 积年 → 局数 → 阴阳遁 → 太乙宫 → 文昌/计神 → 主客算 → 八门 → 天盘星神 → 神盘星神 → 格局 → 九贵神. It consumes the school config from Step 6 and emits the aggregate PanDataModel that holds all five boards from Step 5. Critically, this file has zero Flutter imports — the README's 'algorithm/UI separation' rule is enforced here.

tour.title: School Data — JSON-Driven Configuration
tour.description: The three JSON files in assets/schools encode each school's deity tables, palace mappings, and rule overrides. Notice from the fan-out ranking that these JSON assets are the top three most-connected source nodes in the entire codebase (21–22 outgoing edges each) — they configure nearly every algorithm decision. official_json_repository.dart is the loader: it reads the bundled assets and hands SchoolConfig objects back to the engine from Step 6, completing the data → strategy → calculator pipeline.
tour.languageLesson: Flutter bundles asset files declared in pubspec.yaml and exposes them via `rootBundle.loadString()`. JSON-driven config like this swaps recompiles for asset reloads — adding a fourth school becomes 'drop in another JSON' rather than 'fork the calculator'.

tour.title: Presentation — Rendering the Five Boards
tour.description: TaiyiPanPage is the single Flutter page; it subscribes to the controller from Step 3 and rebuilds when state changes. TaiyiPanGrid is the classic radial chart widget — concentric rings, nine palaces, deities labelled in place. PanInfoPanel shows the textual summary alongside it. PieSegmentPainter is the low-level CustomPainter that draws the wedge geometry behind the grid: this is where the visual identity of a Tai Yi chart actually gets drawn pixel-by-pixel.
tour.languageLesson: Flutter's CustomPainter gives you a Canvas with paths, arcs, and transforms — closer to HTML5 Canvas than to React's declarative tree. For a radial chart, you'd use `canvas.drawArc()` plus `canvas.save()/restore()` around rotation transforms, which is exactly the pattern pie_segment_painter applies.

tour.title: Tests as Specification
tour.description: The tests close the loop and act as the project's executable spec. algorithm_engine_test exercises the strategy pattern from Step 6 — proving that swapping school config produces different deity placements. taiyi_pan_calculator_smoke runs the full chain end-to-end against known reference charts. taiyi_year_eye_rules_flutter_test pins down the year-chart 'eye' (主目) rules, which is exactly the kind of cross-school disagreement the README highlights as tricky. If you're about to change a school rule or extend the algorithm, these tests tell you what 'still correct' means.
